summary: USPH presents a defensive-healthcare name in mid-drawdown (-32.2%) with a MIXED disclosure profile. The FY25 10-K shows genuine operating growth (revenue +16.3%, USPH NI +26%, operating income +37.6%) but the immediately-following Q1 2026 10-Q reveals a single-quarter operating inflection (operating income -36%, USPH NI -49%, GAAP EPS $(0.12) vs $0.80). The single most diagnostic finding is the CFO transition under-disclosure: Carey Hendrickson was omitted from the 2026 LTIP eligibility list on March 13, 2026 (effective March 9), disposed of 10,000 shares on March 10, 2026 (code D), and resigned effective April 24, 2026 - yet there is NO standalone 8-K Item 5.02 announcing the resignation; first public disclosure was buried in the Q1 10-Q subsequent-events note (May 8, 2026). Other Mode-B findings: the 60-clinic Metro hospital-alliance conversion (8.9% of network) lacks any revenue/EBITDA bridge; the Q1 dividend ($0.46) was 138% of GAAP NI and funded via $44M revolver draw; share-repurchase authorization sat unused as stock fell below the Nov 2025 buyback price ($68.45); ERP implementation will run through year-end 2026 overlapping CFO transition. Form 4 evidence is mixed: Director Kathleen Gilmartin made TWO legitimate code-P open-market purchases (Sept 2024: $172K; Nov 20 2025: $276K @ $69 INTO the drawdown - a genuine positive signal) but the entire C-suite (CEO/CFO/President/COO) made ZERO code-P purchases over 21 months. The May 20 2026 5-director Form-4 cluster (5 days pre-cutoff) is annual code-A grants at $61.61 fair value, NOT open-market purchases - this is the kind of pattern that could mislead a less-careful reader. Net verdict: NEUTRAL leaning slightly negative - real growth franchise with credible director-buy datapoint (Gilmartin) but multiple Form-S underdisclosures (CFO timing, Metro economics, dividend sustainability) and absence of C-suite conviction-buy at distressed levels. Composite suggests NEUTRAL tier rather than SHORT-tier - the company is not lying about a broken franchise, but it is under-narrating a transition.
